data.name: Hindiyya
data.gender_notes: Hindiyya is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Hind', meaning 'River' or 'Indus', and the suffix '-iyya' meaning 'Goddess'. This name is believed to be derived from the Hindu goddess Indus or Saraswati. The name Hindiyya carries the meaning “Goddess of the River Indus” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hindiyya usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the river indus and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hindiyya belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the River Indus.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hindiyya total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: هندية
in_arabic.meaning: المرأة الهندية، الهنديَّة، المشتقة من الهنديُّ
